# Spec — #488: Guardian/assistant LAN mDNS self-advertisement

_Implementation spec against the current branch (0.13.0-beta.3 baseline), 2026-07-12._
_Source assessment: [`../assessments/488.md`](../assessments/488.md) — spot-checked against
the tree; all cited line references verified (guardian ports at
`packages/skeleton/system/stack/portals.compose.yml:155`, assistant port default at
`packages/skeleton/system/stack/core.compose.yml:98`, `isLoopback` at
`packages/lib/src/control-plane/bind-warning.ts:22`, LAN toggle at
`packages/ui/src/routes/api/host/stack/+server.ts:76-93`, `collectBindAddressWarnings`
call at `packages/ui/src/hooks.server.ts:59`)._

---

## 0. Ratified decisions (the assessment offered options — these are the calls)

**D1 — Advertisement locus: the HOST control-plane process, not the guardian container.**
The issue text says "the guardian … advertise[s]", but D5a
(`docs/technical/network-partitioning-d5a.md:100-111`) proves container mDNS on the
default bridge network never reaches the physical LAN, and `network_mode: host` would
break the partitioning invariants (guardian must stay the sole dual-network broker) and
is inert on macOS anyway. The responder therefore runs inside the long-lived host UI
server process (the SvelteKit child every supervisor — `openpalm ui serve`, `openpalm`,
Electron — spawns), started from `hooks.server.ts`'s one-shot init. This is recorded in
the refreshed d5a doc as the explicit rejection of the in-guardian option. The
`packages/guardian` package is untouched.

**D2 — Base name comes from `OP_PROJECT_NAME`.** There is no structured
"assistant name" (persona is free-text markdown), so the base label is
`sanitizeDnsLabel(OP_PROJECT_NAME ?? "openpalm")` → `openpalm.local` /
`openpalm-guardian.local` by default. The admin-UI hint text names the source
(`OP_PROJECT_NAME`) so users are not surprised that their persona name is not used
(assessment risk 5).

**D3 — The assistant's native OpenCode mDNS block stays as-is (documented
advanced/manual path).** `packages/skeleton/system/assistant/opencode.jsonc` keeps its
static `"mdns": false, "mdnsDomain": "openpalm.local"`. It is NOT file-assembled to the
derived name in this task: the host responder is now the primary (and only
LAN-reachable) advertisement mechanism, the native path is inert on bridge networks,
and #563 (network access presets) already plans post-overwrite file assembly for
`opencode.jsonc` per preset — doing it here would be duplicated, soon-replaced work.
Only the comment block is updated to point at the host responder.

**D4 — Displayed scheme is `http://` for now.** #557 (guardian edge TLS) explicitly
says the mDNS surfacing should show the HTTPS name *once TLS lands*. The GET payload
carries name + port + advertised flag (not a pre-baked URL string), so the UI can
switch the rendered scheme when #557's work lands without an API change. Coordination
note added to the d5a doc.

**D5 — `OP_MDNS` off-switch (non-secret, `stack.env`).** A single opt-out knob
(`OP_MDNS=0|false|off` disables the responder even when binds are non-loopback). It is
a real operator need — coexistence with an already-configured host responder
(avahi/Bonjour publishing conflicting records, assessment risk 1) — not a test-only
flag. Default (unset) = enabled, still fully gated by the bind addresses, so the
default security posture is unchanged.

**D6 — Gating is bind-address-only.** The guardian name is advertised whenever
`OP_BIND_ADDRESS` is set non-loopback, even if no guardian-ingress addon is currently
enabled (the guardian is profile-gated). Checking addon/profile state would couple the
responder to compose state parsing for a purely cosmetic gain (a name that resolves to
a closed port). The issue's acceptance is phrased exactly as bind-gating; keep it.

---

## 1. Scope

### Closes (from the assessment's remaining-work list)

1. **Ratify the advertisement locus + record in d5a** (item 1) → D1 above; d5a doc
   rewrite.
2. **Minimal mDNS responder module in lib** (item 2) →
   `packages/lib/src/control-plane/mdns-responder.ts`, `node:dgram`, pure
   encode/decode/gating functions unit-testable without sockets.
3. **Gating logic** (item 3) → `<base>-guardian.local` only when `OP_BIND_ADDRESS`
   non-loopback (guardian host port `OP_GUARDIAN_PORT`, default 3830);
   `<base>.local` only when `OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS` non-loopback (assistant host
   port `OP_ASSISTANT_PORT`, default 3800 — note the assistant port line does NOT nest
   `OP_BIND_ADDRESS`, per `core.compose.yml:98`). `isLoopback` exported from
   `bind-warning.ts` and reused. Loopback-only default starts **no socket at all**.
4. **Name derivation** (item 4) → D2 + D3 above.
5. **Admin UI surface** (item 5) → `mdns` object on GET/PUT `/api/host/stack`;
   rendered in the LAN Exposure card of `AssistantTab.svelte`.
6. **Tests** (item 6) → §2 below.
7. **Docs** (item 7) → d5a mDNS section rewrite, `environment-and-mounts.md` new vars,
   `core.compose.yml` comment block, CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`.

### Descoped (with justification)

- **IPv6 / AAAA records.** `udp4` socket + A records only. IPv4 mDNS resolution works
  on every mainstream client OS; dual-stack multicast (per-interface `udp6` sockets,
  `ff02::fb`, scope ids) roughly doubles the socket code for no acceptance-criteria
  gain. Recorded in the d5a doc as a known limitation.
- **RFC 6762 §8 probing / name-conflict defense.** We are the only intended publisher
  of these names; full probe/defense state machines are unjustified complexity for a
  convenience advertisement. Conflicts with a foreign publisher are handled by the
  `OP_MDNS` off-switch + documentation.
- **File-assembling `opencode.jsonc` `mdnsDomain` to the derived name** — deferred to
  #563's per-preset file assembly (D3).
- **Surfacing the HTTPS / ts.net name** — #557's scope (D4); the payload shape is
  designed so no API change is needed then.
- **Advertising from a longer-lived host component** (systemd unit etc., assessment
  risk 3). Requires new host-OS infrastructure outside the control plane. Instead the
  limitation ("advertisement lives and dies with the host `openpalm` UI process") is
  documented in d5a and in the admin-UI hint.
- **Advertising portal/addon edge ports (chat 3820, api 3821, voice)** — the issue
  names only the guardian and assistant; per-addon advertisement is #563 territory.

## 2. TEST-FIRST PLAN

Write these before any implementation. All are red initially except where marked
**(pin)** — pin tests assert an existing invariant the new code depends on and may
pass immediately; they exist to fail if the implementation (or a later change) drifts.

### 2.1 `packages/lib/src/control-plane/mdns-responder.test.ts` (NEW — `bun test`, run via `bun run lib:test`)

Idioms to mirror: `bind-warning.test.ts` (plain env-record in/out assertions),
`network-partitioning.test.ts` (socket-free fixture style), and the injected-deps
pattern used across lib (e.g. `apply-stack-di.test.ts`). No real sockets anywhere:
the responder tests use a stub socket factory. **Red reason: the module
`./mdns-responder.js` does not exist — every test fails at import.**

Name derivation:

1. `sanitizeDnsLabel lowercases and maps underscores/invalid chars to hyphens` —
   `sanitizeDnsLabel("My_Lab!")` → `"my-lab"`.
2. `sanitizeDnsLabel trims leading/trailing hyphens and collapses runs` —
   `"--a__b--"` → `"a-b"`.
3. `sanitizeDnsLabel falls back to "openpalm" when nothing survives` — `"___"` →
   `"openpalm"`; `""` → `"openpalm"`.
4. `sanitizeDnsLabel truncates to 54 chars so "-guardian" still fits a 63-char DNS label`.
5. `deriveMdnsNames defaults to openpalm.local / openpalm-guardian.local` — `{}` in.
6. `deriveMdnsNames derives from OP_PROJECT_NAME` — `{ OP_PROJECT_NAME: "my_lab" }` →
   `my-lab.local` / `my-lab-guardian.local`.

Gating truth table (`resolveMdnsAdvertisements(env, hostIpv4)` with injected
`hostIpv4: ["192.168.1.20"]`):

7. `empty env advertises nothing` — `{}` → `[]`.
8. `explicit loopback values advertise nothing` —
   `{ OP_BIND_ADDRESS: "127.0.0.1", OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS: "localhost" }` → `[]`.
9. `OP_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0 advertises the guardian name only` — one advert:
   `{ service: "guardian", name: "openpalm-guardian.local", port: 3830, addresses: ["192.168.1.20"] }`.
10. `OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0 advertises the assistant name only` — port 3800.
11. `both non-loopback advertises both; custom ports respected` —
    `OP_GUARDIAN_PORT=4830`, `OP_ASSISTANT_PORT=4800` show up in the adverts.
12. `a specific bind IP narrows the A-record addresses to that IP` —
    `OP_BIND_ADDRESS: "192.168.1.5"` → guardian `addresses: ["192.168.1.5"]`
    (ignores the injected interface list).
13. `OP_MDNS=off disables everything even with non-loopback binds` — also `"0"`,
    `"false"`.
14. `resolveMdnsStatus reports names/ports with advertised flags` — loopback env →
    both `advertised: false` but names/ports still populated (the UI shows the
    would-be name).

DNS wire format (pure, byte-level — build packets with hand-rolled `Uint8Array`
fixtures in the test file):

15. `parseDnsQuestions decodes a standard A question` — fixture: query for
    `OpenPalm.local` type A class IN → `[{ name: "openpalm.local", type: 1, qclass: 1 }]`
    (name lowercased).
16. `parseDnsQuestions returns null for a response packet (QR=1)`.
17. `parseDnsQuestions returns null for truncated/malformed packets without throwing`
    — empty buffer, header-only, question cut mid-name.
18. `parseDnsQuestions handles a compression pointer without looping forever` — a
    self-pointing pointer fixture must return null (bounded hops), not hang/throw.
19. `buildMdnsAnswer answers an A query for an advertised name` — response has QR+AA
    set, ID 0, one A answer with cache-flush bit (class 0x8001), TTL 120, rdata
    equal to the advert address; the answer name round-trips through
    `parseDnsQuestions`-style decoding of the name bytes.
20. `buildMdnsAnswer answers TYPE_ANY queries for an advertised name`.
21. `buildMdnsAnswer returns null for an unknown name` — no response packet at all.
22. `buildMdnsAnswer matches names case-insensitively`.
23. `buildMdnsAnswer answers a PTR query for _http._tcp.local with SRV/TXT/A additionals`
    — PTR answer per advert pointing at `<label>._http._tcp.local`, SRV target =
    advert name + port, TXT contains `path=/`, A for the advert name in additionals.
24. `buildMdnsGoodbye emits TTL 0 records for every advert`.
25. `preserves the query ID and answers unicast for legacy (non-5353 source) queries`
    — `buildMdnsAnswer(questions, adverts, { queryId: 0x1234 })` carries ID 0x1234.

Responder lifecycle (stub socket factory — an object recording
`bind`/`addMembership`/`send`/`close` calls and exposing an `emitMessage(msg, rinfo)`
hook):

26. `startMdnsResponder returns null and opens no socket when there is nothing to advertise`
    — factory never invoked. **This is the loopback-default-emits-nothing acceptance test.**
27. `startMdnsResponder binds 5353, joins 224.0.0.251, and announces` — with one
    advert: factory called once, `bind` called with port 5353 + `reuseAddr` socket,
    `addMembership("224.0.0.251")` called, at least one announcement `send` to
    `224.0.0.251:5353`.
28. `responder answers a matching query received on the socket` — `emitMessage` with
    the A-query fixture → `send` called with a buffer whose answer decodes to the
    advert address, destination `224.0.0.251:5353`.
29. `responder ignores non-matching and malformed messages` — no `send`.
30. `stop() sends goodbye and closes the socket`.
31. `socket errors are non-fatal` — factory throws / stub emits `error` →
    `startMdnsResponder` returns null (or the handle goes inert) and does not throw.

Reconcile (temp `homeDir` with a seeded `knowledge/env/stack.env`, stub factory via
`deps`):

32. `reconcileMdnsResponder starts nothing for a loopback stack.env` — factory unused.
33. `reconcileMdnsResponder starts the responder when stack.env enables LAN exposure`
    — write `OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0`, reconcile → factory called;
    returned `MdnsStatus.assistant.advertised === true`.
34. `reconcile is idempotent for an unchanged env` — second call: no new socket, no
    stop.
35. `reconcile stops the responder when the env returns to loopback` — goodbye sent +
    close called.
36. `process.env OP_MDNS=0 force-disables reconcile regardless of stack.env` —
    (pass `processEnv` via deps to keep the test hermetic).

## 3. File-level changes

### 3.1 `packages/lib/src/control-plane/mdns-responder.ts` (NEW)

Single module, `node:dgram` + `node:os` only (no new dependency — Bun implements
`node:dgram`; the module also runs under the UI's adapter-node process). Structured
logging via `import { createLogger } from "../logger.js"` (`createLogger("mdns")`),
matching `setup.ts`/`akm-sources.ts`. Layout: pure section first (no imports with
side effects), socket section second, reconcile singleton last.

Constants: `MDNS_ADDR = "224.0.0.251"`, `MDNS_PORT = 5353`, `TYPE_A = 1`,
`TYPE_PTR = 12`, `TYPE_TXT = 16`, `TYPE_SRV = 33`, `TYPE_ANY = 255`,
`CLASS_IN = 1`, cache-flush bit `0x8000`, `TTL = 120`,
`HTTP_SERVICE = "_http._tcp.local"`, `DEFAULT_GUARDIAN_PORT = 3830`,
`DEFAULT_ASSISTANT_PORT = 3800`.

Pure exports (exact signatures):

```ts
export function sanitizeDnsLabel(raw: string, maxLength = 54): string;
export function deriveMdnsNames(env: Record<string, string | undefined>): {
  base: string; assistantName: string; guardianName: string;
};
export type MdnsAdvertisement = {
  service: "assistant" | "guardian";
  /** lowercase FQDN, e.g. "openpalm-guardian.local" */
  name: string;
  /** host TCP port (OP_GUARDIAN_PORT / OP_ASSISTANT_PORT defaults) */
  port: number;
  /** IPv4 addresses for A answers */
  addresses: string[];
};
export function resolveMdnsAdvertisements(
  env: Record<string, string | undefined>,
  hostIpv4?: string[],           // default: non-internal IPv4s from os.networkInterfaces()
): MdnsAdvertisement[];
export type MdnsStatus = {
  assistant: { name: string; port: number; advertised: boolean };
  guardian: { name: string; port: number; advertised: boolean };
};
export function resolveMdnsStatus(env: Record<string, string | undefined>): MdnsStatus;
export type DnsQuestion = { name: string; type: number; qclass: number };
export function parseDnsQuestions(msg: Uint8Array): DnsQuestion[] | null;
export function buildMdnsAnswer(
  questions: DnsQuestion[],
  adverts: MdnsAdvertisement[],
  opts?: { queryId?: number },
): Uint8Array | null;
export function buildMdnsAnnouncement(adverts: MdnsAdvertisement[]): Uint8Array | null;
export function buildMdnsGoodbye(adverts: MdnsAdvertisement[]): Uint8Array | null;
```

Semantics:

- `sanitizeDnsLabel`: trim → lowercase → every char outside `[a-z0-9-]` (incl. `_`)
  becomes `-` → collapse `-` runs → strip leading/trailing `-` → truncate to
  `maxLength` → `"openpalm"` if empty. 54 leaves room for `-guardian` (9 chars)
  inside the 63-char label limit.
- `resolveMdnsAdvertisements` gate: disabled entirely when
  `env.OP_MDNS` trims/lowercases to `"0" | "false" | "off" | "no"`. Guardian advert
  iff `env.OP_BIND_ADDRESS` is set and `!isLoopback(it)`; assistant advert iff
  `env.OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS` is set and non-loopback (no `OP_BIND_ADDRESS`
  fallback — mirrors `core.compose.yml:98`). Unset ⇒ compose default 127.0.0.1 ⇒ no
  advert. Addresses: if the bind value is a specific IP (not `0.0.0.0`/`::`), use
  `[bindValue]`; otherwise the `hostIpv4` list. An advert with zero addresses is
  dropped. Reuses `isLoopback` imported from `./bind-warning.js`.
- Encoder: no name compression (legal per RFC 1035; keeps the encoder ~trivial).
  Answers are multicast-shaped (ID 0) unless `opts.queryId` is passed (legacy
  unicast reply). A answers carry the cache-flush bit; PTR answers for
  `HTTP_SERVICE` list one instance `<label from name minus .local>._http._tcp.local`
  per advert with SRV/TXT/A in the additional section (fixes the `opencode-4096`
  friendly-label gap for host-advertised names). `TYPE_ANY` matches A for hostnames
  and PTR for the service name.
- Parser: header + question section only, defensive: bounds-checked, compression
  pointers followed with a hop limit (e.g. 16), returns `null` on QR=1 or any
  malformation. Input is `Uint8Array` (untrusted network bytes — never `any`).

Socket layer:

```ts
export type MdnsRemoteInfo = { address: string; port: number };
export type MdnsSocketLike = {
  bind(port: number, address: string, cb?: () => void): void;
  addMembership(mcastAddr: string): void;
  setMulticastTTL(ttl: number): void;
  send(msg: Uint8Array, port: number, address: string): void;
  close(): void;
  on(event: "message", cb: (msg: Uint8Array, rinfo: MdnsRemoteInfo) => void): void;
  on(event: "error", cb: (err: Error) => void): void;
  unref?(): void;
};
export type MdnsSocketFactory = () => MdnsSocketLike;
export type MdnsResponderHandle = { stop(): void };
export function startMdnsResponder(
  adverts: MdnsAdvertisement[],
  deps: { createSocket?: MdnsSocketFactory } = {},
): MdnsResponderHandle | null;
```

- `adverts.length === 0` ⇒ return `null` **before** touching the factory (the
  loopback-default "no socket at all" guarantee).
- Default factory: `dgram.createSocket({ type: "udp4", reuseAddr: true })`
  (`reuseAddr` is what lets us coexist with avahi/Bonjour on 5353). Bind
  `0.0.0.0:5353`; on listening: `addMembership(MDNS_ADDR)`, `setMulticastTTL(255)`,
  `unref?.()` (never keeps the process alive), send the announcement twice (second
  via an unref'd 1 s timer, per RFC 6762 startup guidance).
- `message` handler: `parseDnsQuestions` → `buildMdnsAnswer`; reply multicast to
  `224.0.0.251:5353` for standard (source port 5353) queries, unicast to
  `rinfo.address:rinfo.port` with the original query ID for legacy queries.
- All failures (bind EADDRINUSE/EACCES, membership errors, send errors) are logged
  `warn` with the advert names and swallowed — advertisement is a convenience and
  must never take the UI server down (fail-open for the convenience, fail-closed
  for the gate). `stop()`: send goodbye (best-effort), `close()`.

Reconcile singleton (explicit, documented owner — mirrors `hooks.server.ts`'s
`startupApplyDone` one-shot pattern; "no hidden global state" satisfied by a single
module-scoped `active: { key: string; handle: MdnsResponderHandle } | null` whose
ownership is this module only):

```ts
export function reconcileMdnsResponder(
  homeDir: string,
  deps: {
    env?: Record<string, string | undefined>;        // default readStackEnv(homeDir)
    processEnv?: Record<string, string | undefined>; // default process.env (OP_MDNS force-off only)
    createSocket?: MdnsSocketFactory;
    hostIpv4?: string[];
  } = {},
): MdnsStatus;
export function _setMdnsSocketFactoryForTests(factory: MdnsSocketFactory | null): void;
export function _resetMdnsResponderForTests(): void; // stop (no goodbye) + clear singleton
```

- Reads `readStackEnv(homeDir)` **fresh on every call** (never process.env for the
  gate vars — hooks.server.ts's startup promotion is only-if-unset and would go
  stale after a PUT). The single process-env exception: `OP_MDNS` in `processEnv`
  force-disables (operator/test kill switch), checked alongside the stack.env value.
- Computes adverts, serializes them to a comparison key; unchanged key ⇒ no-op.
  Changed ⇒ `stop()` the old handle (goodbye) and `startMdnsResponder` the new set
  (respecting `_setMdnsSocketFactoryForTests` if installed). Never throws: wraps
  the socket work in try/catch + `logger.warn`. Returns `resolveMdnsStatus` of the
  effective env so route handlers can echo it.

### 3.6 `packages/ui/src/lib/api/akm.ts` (MODIFY, lines 55-72)

Extend the shared types (the `mdns` shape is defined once here and reused):

```ts
export type MdnsSurface = {
  assistant: { name: string; port: number; advertised: boolean };
  guardian: { name: string; port: number; advertised: boolean };
};
export type HostStackSettings = {
  projectName: string;
  lanExposureEnabled: boolean;
  stackEnvPath: string;
  mdns: MdnsSurface;
};
```

and add `mdns: MdnsSurface` to `saveHostStackSettings`'s return type.

## 4. Acceptance mapping

| Issue acceptance criterion | Proof |
|---|---|
| 1. mDNS responder baked (no boot-time `apk add`) | Already structurally met (avahi sidecars removed; pinned by existing `network-partitioning.test.ts:191-204`). This task adds the actual responder as lib code in the host process — no container, no image, no `apk` at all. Artifact: `mdns-responder.ts` + test 27 (bind/membership/announce with zero shell-outs). |
| 2. Advertises only when LAN access is enabled; loopback-only default emits nothing | Gating truth-table tests 7-13; no-socket-at-all tests 26 & 32; reconcile flip tests 33-35; compose-reality pins 38-39; UI-side tests 40-41, 43. |
| 3. Admin UI surfaces the `.local` name when enabled | Payload tests 40-44 (`mdns` on GET/PUT `/api/host/stack`); `AssistantTab.svelte` LAN Exposure card render (§3.7), type-checked by `bun run ui:check`; manual verification step below. |

## 5. Verification gates (implementer must run green, at stage 4 and after every fix round)

- `bun run lint`
- `bun run check`
- `bun run lib:test`
- `bun run cli:test`
- `bun run ui:check`
- Additionally (the suite that contains the new vitest cases): `bun run ui:test:unit`

Known sandbox flakes (root-uid ownership tests in lib) are compared against the
pre-change baseline, not treated as regressions.

Manual/e2e verification (not CI-gated; record the result in the PR/commit body): on a
Linux host with `OP_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0`, `avahi-resolve -n openpalm-guardian.local`
(or `dns-sd -G v4 openpalm-guardian.local` on macOS) from another LAN machine
resolves; with the loopback default, `ss -ulpn | grep 5353` shows no socket owned by
the openpalm process.

---

## 6. Risks (from the assessment) and how the design avoids them

1. **Hand-rolled multicast DNS is fiddly (5353 sharing, EADDRINUSE, silent
   non-answers).** Pure encode/decode is byte-tested (tests 15-25) without sockets;
   the socket layer is a thin, injectable shell (tests 26-31). `reuseAddr: true`
   coexists with avahi/Bonjour; every socket failure is a logged warn, never a crash;
   `OP_MDNS=off` is the operator escape hatch for pathological hosts. Legacy-unicast
   handling (test 25) covers simple resolvers.
2. **Architecture divergence from the issue text (in-guardian vs host).** Decided
   (D1) and recorded in the d5a doc with the bridge-multicast rationale — the spec
   review is the sign-off point the assessment asks for.
3. **Host UI process not guaranteed running while the stack is.** Descoped from code;
   documented in d5a and in the AssistantTab hint ("broadcast by the host `openpalm`
   process while it runs"). The socket is `unref`'d so it also never *prolongs* the
   process.
4. **Fail-closed gating (never advertise on the loopback default).** The no-advert ⇒
   no-socket guarantee is enforced before the socket factory is even consulted
   (test 26), the gate reads stack.env fresh on every reconcile (never stale
   process.env), and the truth table (tests 7-13, 32-36, 40-44) covers every
   combination including force-off. Compose pins 38-39 keep the gate vars honest.
5. **`OP_PROJECT_NAME` may surprise users expecting the persona name.** Hint text in
   the LAN Exposure card names the source var (§3.7); d5a records the rationale (no
   structured assistant name exists).
6. **`opencode-4096` instance label if the native path is kept.** The host responder
   advertises friendly `_http._tcp` instance labels (test 23), so the cosmetic
   regression now only exists on the manual/advanced native path — noted in d5a.

---

## 7. Out of scope (explicit)

- Any change to `packages/guardian` or the guardian container/image.
- IPv6 (AAAA, `ff02::fb`) advertisement.
- RFC 6762 probing / conflict defense.
- File-assembling `opencode.jsonc` `server.mdns`/`mdnsDomain` to the derived name
  (deferred to #563 preset wiring).
- HTTPS/ts.net name surfacing and any TLS work (#557).
- Advertising chat/api/voice addon edge ports (#563).
- A standalone/long-lived host advertisement daemon (systemd/launchd).
- `@openpalm/client` changes of any kind.
- New runtime dependencies or `bun.lock` changes.
